rm -rf data && (PORT=3456 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1 && cat /tmp/server.log

echo "--- stored file"
cat data/books.json
echo "--- finish first book"

(PORT=3456 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1

echo "--- book page"
curl -s localhost:3456/books/$ID | sed -e 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -12
pkill -f "node server.mjs"

args.content:
# Bookshelf

A tiny app for keeping track of the books you're reading. No accounts, no database — books are saved to `data/books.json`.

```sh
npm start        # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

Set `PORT` to change the port and `BOOKS_FILE` to store the JSON file somewhere else.

## Pages

- `/` — what you're currently reading, what you've finished, and a form to add a book.
- `/books/<id>` — one book: title, author, notes, a "Mark as finished" button and a notes editor. This URL is shareable.

events.content:
The app is built and verified: `npm start` runs it at http://localhost:3000, and all 15 tests pass with `npm test`.

## What you get

**Home page (`/`)** shows two lists — *Currently reading* and *Finished* (most recently finished first) — followed by an *Add a book* form with title, author and notes. Each list entry links to the book's page.

**Book page (`/books/<id>`)** shows the title, author, when you started or finished it, and your notes. There's a *Mark as finished* button (which disappears once finished), a small form to edit notes, and the page's own URL displayed so you can copy it and send it to someone. Anyone with the link can open it, since there are no accounts.

**Storage** is a single `data/books.json` file, created on first add. Writes go to a temp file and are renamed into place, so a crash mid-save can't corrupt the file. I confirmed the books come back after stopping and restarting the server. `PORT` and `BOOKS_FILE` environment variables override the defaults.

## How it's built

There are no runtime dependencies — it's plain Node with the built-in `http` module and server-rendered HTML, so there's no build step and nothing to install beyond what was already there (vitest for tests).

- `server.mjs` — starts the server
- `src/store.mjs` — loads/saves the JSON file; add, finish, update notes
- `src/app.mjs` — the HTTP routes
- `src/html.mjs` — page templates, with all user content HTML-escaped
- `test/` — store tests (including the restart scenario) and end-to-end HTTP tests against a real listening server

One small addition beyond what you asked for: the notes are editable from the book page, since notes tend to grow while you read. The `data/` directory isn't in `.gitignore`, so you can choose whether to commit your book list or add it there yourself. Nothing has been committed.

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" -X POST localhost:3456/books -d "title=Piranesi&author=Susanna Clarke"
echo "--- stored file"
cat data/books.json
echo "--- finish first book"
ID=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('data/books.json'))[0].id)")
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" -X POST localhost:3456/books/$ID/finish
echo "--- restart"
pkill -f "node server.mjs"; sleep 0.5
(PORT=3456 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
echo "--- home page after restart (text only)"
curl -s localhost:3456/ | sed -e 's/<style>.*<\/style>//' | sed -e 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -v '^\s*$'
echo "--- book page"
curl -s localhost:3456/books/$ID | sed -e 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -12
pkill -f "node server.mjs"

cd /workspace
PORT=3456 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!; sleep 1
ID=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('data/books.json'))[0].id)")
echo "--- home page after restart (tags stripped)"
curl -s localhost:3456/ | sed -e 's/<style>.*<\/style>//' | tr '\n' ' ' | sed -e 's/<style>.*<\/style>//' -e 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' -e 's/  */ /g'
echo; echo "--- book page (tags stripped)"
curl -s localhost:3456/books/$ID | tr '\n' ' ' | sed -e 's/<style>.*<\/style>//' -e 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' -e 's/  */ /g'
echo; echo "--- 404"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" localhost:3456/books/missing
kill $PID
